pr_title: opt: generate constrained partial index scans
pr_body:
This commit updates the GenerateConstrainedScans exploration rule so
that constrained partial index scans are now generated. For example,
consider the following index and query:

    CREATE INDEX ON t (a) WHERE b = 'foo'
    SELECT a FROM t WHERE b = 'foo' and a > 0 AND a < 10

GenerateConstrainedScans will generate the following query plan:

    project
     └── index-join t
          └── scan t@t_a_idx,partial
               └── constraint: /1/3: [/1 - /9]

The statistics builder and logical props builder were also updated to
correctly to correctly account for constrained partial index scans.

Fixes #50231 

Release note: None

Previously, mgartner (Marcus Gartner) wrote…
But it should take into account the index predicate `s IN ('foo', 'bar', 'baz')`. Even though the scan is over `[/216/'baz' - /229/'baz']` its not over _all_ rows in that range, only over rows where s is `foo`, `bar`, or `baz`. Are you sure this isn't correct?
Ah! Sorry -- yep, that makes sense to me. `140 * 3/50 = 8.4`

Having non-output columns in `NotNullCols` is a shaky concept IMO. How do you define NotNullCols precisely? Currently it's pretty simple: it's the subset of OutputCols for which this operator is known to not produce NULLs.

I didn't mean for you to remove all changes to the logical props builder -- I think all your changes are good except for the removal of the line to intersect with OutputCols.

This is an interesting case because this appears to be the first time that columns can be guaranteed to be not null even though they aren't in the set out output cols. For example, if the partial index `INDEX (a) WHERE b > 0` is used for a scan, `b` is guaranteed to be non-null for any row returned by the scan, even though `b` is not contained in the index (hence not an output col).

If I add this line back in, it alters the stats for partial index scans such that they are slightly off. Notice in the example below the scan estimates ~25.1 rows while the index-join (originally a Select in that memo group) estimates ~24.8 rows. 

```
exec-ddl
CREATE INDEX idx ON a (i) WHERE s IN ('foo', 'bar', 'baz')
----

opt
SELECT * FROM a WHERE i > 10 AND i < 20 AND s IN ('foo', 'bar', 'baz')
----
index-join a
 ├── columns: k:1(int!null) i:2(int!null) s:3(string!null) t:4(string)
 ├── stats: [rows=24.8207143, distinct(2)=9, null(2)=0, distinct(3)=3, null(3)=0, distinct(2,3)=24.8207143, null(2,3)=0]
 ├── key: (1)
 ├── fd: (1)-->(2-4)
 └── scan a@idx,partial
      ├── columns: k:1(int!null) i:2(int!null)
      ├── constraint: /2/1: [/11 - /19]
      ├── stats: [rows=25.1421429, distinct(2)=9, null(2)=0, distinct(3)=3, null(3)=25.1421429, distinct(2,3)=25.1421429, null(2,3)=0]
      ├── key: (1)
      └── fd: (1)-->(2)
```

Without this line, the stats are more accurate:

```
exec-ddl
CREATE INDEX idx ON a (i) WHERE s IN ('foo', 'bar', 'baz')
----

opt
SELECT * FROM a WHERE i > 10 AND i < 20 AND s IN ('foo', 'bar', 'baz')
----
index-join a
 ├── columns: k:1(int!null) i:2(int!null) s:3(string!null) t:4(string)
 ├── stats: [rows=24.8207143, distinct(2)=9, null(2)=0, distinct(3)=3, null(3)=0, distinct(2,3)=24.8207143, null(2,3)=0]
 ├── key: (1)
 ├── fd: (1)-->(2-4)
 └── scan a@idx,partial
      ├── columns: k:1(int!null) i:2(int!null)
      ├── constraint: /2/1: [/11 - /19]
      ├── stats: [rows=24.8207143, distinct(2)=9, null(2)=0, distinct(3)=3, null(3)=0, distinct(2,3)=24.8207143, null(2,3)=0]
      ├── key: (1)
      └── fd: (1)-->(2)
```
